title: Mythology
description: A figure the world believes in, as distinct from one it can meet. Kept apart from `characters` on purpose: whether these are real inside the fiction is a question the fiction declines to answer, and the schema should not answer it either.

domain.description: What the figure governs. A list because most govern several.

aspect.description: The face this figure shows -- the same power can be a protector or a devourer.

relations.description: Named ties to other figures, keyed by the nature of the tie. Free-form on purpose: the relationships in a mythology are not a fixed set, and one of the three uses it.

canon.description: How firmly this is established. `primary` is stated by the source material, `inferred` is a reading canon has committed to.
